headline: Grammar Error Detection Game for ESL Proofreading Practice
outcomes: Students sharpen proofreading skills by identifying real grammar errors hidden in authentic-looking paragraphs
Build grammatical intuition — the sense that something is wrong before being able to name the rule
Develop attention to detail in reading, a critical skill for exam preparation and professional writing
Practise applying grammar rules in context rather than in isolated exercise formats
howItWorks: The AI writes a short paragraph on your chosen topic containing a set number of deliberate grammar errors
Students read the paragraph on their device and identify the errors — tapping or marking suspected mistakes
After submissions, the teacher reveals all errors with explanations on the classroom board
Points are awarded for each correctly identified error; false positives (marking correct text) reduce scores
teacherUseCases: Exam preparation for Cambridge, IELTS, or TOEFL writing correction tasks
Review of recently taught grammar rules in an applied, reading context
Engagement hook before corrective feedback — students become error-hunters rather than passive receivers

faq.q: What types of errors does the AI include?
faq.a: The AI can embed a mix of error types: subject-verb agreement, wrong tense, missing articles, incorrect prepositions, and word form errors. You can also ask the AI to focus on one error type by setting the topic.

faq.q: How many errors are in each paragraph?
faq.a: Typically 3–6 errors depending on difficulty. Easy paragraphs have obvious errors; hard paragraphs have subtle, exam-level mistakes that require close grammatical knowledge.

faq.q: Do students need to install anything?
faq.a: Nothing to install. Students access Error Hunter on their phone or tablet through any modern browser. A shared link from the teacher is all they need — no app, no student account.

faq.q: Is this suitable for all levels?
faq.a: Easy difficulty suits B1 students with common grammar errors. Hard difficulty uses C1-level subtleties appropriate for advanced exam classes.

faq.q: How much does Error Hunter cost?
faq.a: Error Hunter is completely free. Teachers start a session in under a minute and students join through their browser — no subscription or account required.
